carry_forward_findings.summary: ExecutionLogProvider is a placeholder. The real re-export ships in REC-C3.3 once the cyclic dep with chronos_log is resolved (split NewExecutionRecord into domain or move ExecutionLogBackend wholesale).

chronos_domain::session_id::SessionId is structurally identical to chronos_log::SessionId but they are NOT type-equivalent. REC-C3.3 services-inversion introduces a domain-side alias to chronos_log::SessionId.
ports/* are abstract targets only. chronos-services still consumes concrete adapters (SegmentedExecutionLog). REC-C3.3 inverts services -> ports; today HEX-002 is gap (its closure criterion).

Framework finding: sddk release apply --route local requires permissions.yaml at the repo root, but manually orchestrated repos can legitimately lack one. Today rec-c3-1 used a workaround (direct git tag + receipts + transition --gate-receipt). Tracked outside the product.
carry_forward_findings.rationale: Repro is deterministic. Resolution should land as a simplify-and-realign step in any cycle that touches crates/sddk-cli/src/release.rs, NOT inside chronos product cycles. Carries forward into framework backlog until release-apply either (a) treats permissions.yaml as optional for --route local or (b) exposes --permit-unscoped-release.

next_cycle_recommendation: Open REC-C3.2 (hexagonal boundary: extract webhook infrastructure out of chronos_domain). Three mechanical invariants should anchor the cycle from the first commit: HEX-C32-01 chronos_domain MUST NOT depend on HTTP/webhook adapter crates; HEX-C32-02 domain source MUST NOT import HTTP client/URL/retry infrastructure; HEX-C32-03 services/application may depend on NotificationSink, not on a concrete webhook implementation. UAT for substitutability: same use case through InMemoryNotificationSink AND WebhookNotificationSink, both pass. Do not roll C31-DEBT-01..03 into C3.2 — those belong to REC-C3.3 (services-inversion). Do not start REC-C3.2 unless explicitly greenlit by the operator; today is a checkpoint, not a cycle.
